unresolved_added: Straight, smooth, obstacle-free, weather-free highways omit major capacity and safety conditions.
One fixed edge dedicated lane and compulsory SDV use predetermine part of the policy result.
Perfect legal compliance removes common speed, stopping, shoulder and signaling behavior.
Traffic accidents are omitted although later policy claims invoke accident reduction.
Average daily traffic suppresses peak, direction and day variability.
Perfect Internet sharing and network decision making omit latency, loss, cybersecurity and partial connectivity.
Malfunctioning SDVs are merely relabeled NSDVs; failure onset and degraded control are not modeled.
Four-meter cells and 1.5-second turns have no joint discretization sensitivity.
One-cell-per-turn speed increments imply a fixed 2.67 m/s^2 acceleration without vehicle-class variation.
Minimum and maximum safe-distance arrays are inputs in code, but their complete derivation and calibration are not released.
P1 values 0.94/0.50/0.20 are transferred from prior work without Seattle-driver validation.
Brake-light and acceleration-state communication assumes correct and instantaneous observation.
Equation 4.7 subtracts leader braking distance from the follower gap without a collision proof.
The source claim that no collision will happen is stronger than the model and code evidence.
SDV-Train decisions use the first vehicle's action without communication delay or string-stability analysis.
NSDV lane changing discusses left moves and assumes right moves are identical, ignoring lane-specific incentives and exits.
LCM and LCS omit simultaneous conflicts, reservations, mandatory merges and route choice.
The two-step signal/move process does not specify a robust scheduler when conditions change between steps.
NSDV LCP parameters are assumed because they are hard to observe; no fit is reported.
SDVs have no stochastic lane-choice layer, making automated behavior unrealistically deterministic.
Formula glyphs and operators are text-extraction-corrupted; source raster must remain the fidelity authority.
Each Figure 12 point averages six runs, but no seed, run variance or interval is reported.
Tipping points are marked visually with red crosses without an algorithm or uncertainty.
The approximately 14 mph equilibrium is a congestion floor, not a demonstrated dynamical equilibrium.
The near-tripling capacity result depends on perfect SDV cooperation and the selected gap arrays.
The 50-percent lane-efficiency minimum has a plausible train-formation story but no diagnostic or statistical test.
Reference 10 is a bridge-presence paper and appears weakly related to highway lane-changing interference.
Figure 18 contains lane-count-specific crossovers, but later prose turns them into one approximately 30-percent policy threshold.
Forcing all SDVs into one dedicated lane mechanically causes the high-share decline.
Actual traffic flow and simulated safe-law capacity may differ in time window, direction and measurement basis.
Actual flow above a simulated curve does not prove overspeed or unsafe following distance.
The source alternates Interstate 402 and 405; the intended road identity must be reconciled.
All-SDV capacity still leaves residual shortfalls, but road widening and network redesign are not optimized or costed.
LCP sensitivity changes one parameter at a time and does not test interactions or distributional uncertainty.
Table 3 likely contains decimal errors: +4.7/-7.9 percent should be near +0.47/-0.79 percent from the displayed times.
Speed-limit variation demonstrates model responsiveness, not robustness or empirical specificity.
The source calls slight parameter response good sensitivity, conflating sensitivity and robustness.
Conclusion and letter use a universal 30-percent lane threshold more firmly than Figure 18 supports.
Technology-company funding, road widening and network redesign advice lacks economic, equity and implementation analysis.
MATLAB and C++ code uses time-based random seeding and releases no input files or environment, so results are not reproducible.
Displayed C++ fixes dedicated_lane=0; the dedicated-lane figures require an unrecorded rebuild or different source.
Code variable kindpossibility appears to encode NSDV probability while plots use SDV percentage; inversion risk is unresolved.
Modulo-based random draws can be biased and their exact probability semantics are unclear.
The displayed data-collection loop covers lane numbers four and five in that build, while figures report one through five lanes.
Code logs collisions but the paper assumes accidents absent; handling a detected collision is not specified.
No held-out detector validation, uncertainty propagation, costs, induced demand, adoption dynamics or monitoring and reversal rule is supplied.
